dossier.title: Database failover incident: 45 minute outage
dossier.subtitle: Primary database became unavailable. Failover to replica succeeded. RCA identified replication lag detection failure.

pages.title: Summary
pages.summary: What happened and what we did about it.

blocks.text: At 2026-10-08T14:32Z, our primary PostgreSQL database became unresponsive. Automated failover detected the issue at T+8 minutes and promoted the standby replica. Service was fully restored at T+45 minutes.
Failover detection was slower than the SLA of 5 minutes because replication lag checks were not running.

items.label: Primary becomes unresponsive
items.body: Connection pool starts timing out on all queries.

items.label: Alerting fires
items.body: On-call team is paged. Application error rate reaches 95%.

items.label: Manual investigation begins
items.body: Team connects to replica, checks replication lag. Shows 20ms lag, which is normal.

items.label: Failover automation triggers
items.body: After 10 minutes of primary unavailability, the automatic failover script promotes the replica.

items.label: Application reconnects
items.body: Application detects replica is now primary and failover config propagates.

items.label: All traffic restored
items.body: Last customer reconnects. Error rate returns to baseline.

pages.title: Root cause
pages.summary: Why the primary went down and how we could have detected it sooner.

blocks.text: The primary database ran out of disk space at 14:32Z. The event was not detected because disk usage monitoring had a 15-minute resolution, so it missed the spike.
We got lucky: the replica was caught up and promoted cleanly. If replication had lagged, we would have lost 20 minutes of recent writes.

pages.title: Action items
pages.summary: What we are doing to prevent this.

items.text: Add disk usage alert with 1-minute resolution and 80% threshold
Restore replication lag detection script and test in staging
Reduce failover detection timeout from 10 to 5 minutes
Set up automatic disk cleanup for old log files
